paper_title: Keeping Futures Contestable: How Editable Artefacts and Evaluation Protocols Shape Speculative Quality
central_problem: AI-mediated speculative artefacts may become difficult to contest during making and prematurely closed during evaluation.
target_venue: Interacting with Computers special issue: The Quality of Speculation in HCI
target_readers: HCI researchers in speculative design; human-AI interaction; design evaluation
field_positioning: Treat speculative quality as a cross-stage property of making and judgement rather than a final-output score.
core_gap: The field lacks direct evidence linking representational editability, evaluation protocol, and the continued contestability of embedded sociotechnical assumptions.
current_dominant_narrative: Quality is commonly evaluated at the final artefact or through one rubric.
narrative_to_correct: Technical validity, interpretive openness, and curatorial value are related but non-interchangeable warrants across a trajectory.
why_now: Generative production and automated evaluation increase the risk of invisible assumptions and construct-invalid closure.
boundary_statement: Claims are limited to recruited participants, three visual micro-speculations, two implemented making workflows, two implemented evaluation protocols, and the frozen coding process.
success_criterion: Complete traceable human Study A and Study B datasets; pass construct checks; report technical-curatorial conflicts without a composite score.
notes: Author approved fusion of directions 1, 3, and 4 on 2026-08-27; human evidence is not yet available.
